sections.label: sec:small-area
sections.content: Uniform q, alpha, h and area cutoff; Jacobi lower metric estimate; regional two-radius focusing and local-inverse self-return; cyclic factor-two cover; losses L/50, 3L/50 and L/10; almost-everywhere outer endpoints; smooth approximation and closed-C2 trimming with turning margins 1/200, 3/400 and 7/800.

sections.background_classification: General weak compactness and elliptic regularity are background; phase retention, modulus confinement, boundary-label transport, affine-phase immersion, cyclic regional geometry and trimmed intrinsic transport are constructed mathematics. Lemaire Theorem 1.7 alone imposes pi2=0 and Jordan-boundary hypotheses absent from the public statement; it does not replace the specialized construction.

sections.label: sec:annular-confined-focusing

sections.label: sec:static-approximation

sections.label: sec:width-deformation

sections.label: sec:swept-area

sections.label: sec:annular-plateau

sections.label: sec:annular-disk-beltrami

definitions_and_hypotheses_checked: M64Annulus uses the actual fixed rectangle, exact periodic boundary maps, Lipschitz and almost-everywhere manifold differentiability fields, and integrable Jacobian; no minimizer is built into the class.

M64 evolution assumes an initial annulus and degree-one positive lifts only for the evolving branch; the later static ramp comparison allows arbitrary positive degree and has a separate threshold order.
The forward derivative coefficient uses the full curvature supremum, while the exponential comparison uses the distinct M63 unit-input constant K0.
Static family approximation quantifies the threshold before N and family member; finite nets choose one node before circumference and retain it for all smaller circumferences.
M65 raw input requires t0 <= t1, compactness, Hausdorff and second-countable structure, and a pointwise null continuous C1 loop family.
The terminal M65 alternative is pointwise in the sphere parameter and uses the exact integrating-factor profile; no attained width or minimizing family is assumed.
Interior swept annuli require a < s <= t < b; endpoint estimates are obtained separately by fixed-metric filling-area continuity.

substantive_proof_mechanisms.mechanism: Square-root Jacobian nonnegativity, rank-one factorization for zero-area collars, and sInf order inequalities.

Finite sampling on compact C1 sets, unique geodesic side maps, geodesic annulus interpolation, raw disk witnesses, fixed-profile flattening, and finite node net.
Smooth time transition, column-norm/Jacobian bound, projected annulus, two directional disk gluing, Ricci metric transport, and endpoint continuity.
Projected length contraction, energy-good time, finite minimum of node cutoffs, common circumference, class-preserving projected family, and zero-duration case split.
